properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 1000322 - Medium Affected: OTHER - Suspected Responsible Party: TAHOE BOATS
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1000322
Incident Time: 2012-01-12 17:30:00
Nearest City: Manor, TX
Location: BOAT REPAIR FACILITY GROUNDS. IN AN AREA OUTSIDE OF THE MAIN STRUCTURE 15001 E. HWY 290
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: STYRENE
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party: TAHOE BOATS
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 30.327812, -97.545324 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 261.82 gallons
Report Description
LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT UNITS WERE CALLED TO AN ODOR INVESTIGATION AT APPROX 15800 BLK OF HWY 290. THIS FACILITY HAS KNOWN CHEMICALS ON SITE INCLUDING AMMONIA AND THE REPORTS WERE THAT THE "GARLIC-LIKE" ODOR WAS COMING FROM THE STORE. THE LOCAL FD INITIATED A HAZMAT TEAM RESPONSE. THE FD ARRIVED AND WORKED TO MONITOR THE INCIDENT AREA AND FOUND NO SIGNS OF LEAKING MATERIALS AT THIS ADDRESS. WHILE DRIVING THE AREA, THERE WAS A DISCOVERY OF THE SMELL IN A LOW-LYING AREA AND DETERMINED THAT THE SMELL WAS COMING FROM A BOAT REPAIR FACILITY. AT APPROX. 0230 HOURS, CREWS MADE ACCESS TO THE FACILITY AND FOUND THE SOURCE OF THE SMELL. THERE WAS BREACH OF AN APPROX. 265 GALLON TOTE CONTAINER OF UN2055; STYRENE MONOMER. THE LEAK COVERED AN AREA OF APPROX. 35 SQ FT. THE CONTAINER SHOWED A YELLOWISH COLORED LIQUID LEAKING FROM A HOLE THAT WAS LIKELY CAUSED BY CONTACT WITH A TRAILER. ONCE THE SOURCE WAS IDENTIFIED, ALL PERSONS WERE MOVED OUT OF THE IMMEDIATE AREA AND THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY WAS CONTACTED FOR CLEANUP. THE HAZMAT TEAM CLEARED THE SCENE AND LOCAL FD REMAINED ONSCENE TO CONTROL ACCESS UNTIL THE CLEANUP CREW ARRIVED.

Report Description
CALLER IS REPORTING THAT WHILE PREPARING FOR HURRICANE ISAAC THEY PUMPED IN 2,000 BARRELS OF LAKE WATER INTO BALLAST TANKS. THE BALLAST TANKS HAVE BEEN SLOWLY PUMPED OUT SINCE THE HURRICANE. THEY SHOULD HAVE RECOVERED 50 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL MATERIAL OUT OF THE PORT 4 AND STARBOARD 4 TANKS AND THEY ONLY RECOVERED ABOUT 18 BARRELS. THERE WAS DAMAGE SUSTAINED TO THOSE TANKS. THE TANKS WERE EMPTIED OUT SLOWLY FROM YESTERDAY TO TODAY. THERE IS NO SHEEN OR MATERIAL VISIBLE IN THE WATER. THEY ESTIMATE A LOSS OF 32 BARRELS OF CRUDE OIL. THERE WERE ALSO ABOUT 10 EMPTY DRUMS THAT WERE TIED TO THE PLATFORM THAT WERE LOST IN THE STORM. 6-7 DRUMS WERE PLASTIC AND 3 DRUMS WERE STEEL. 4 DRUMS HAVE "JW" STENCILED ON THE SIDE, THE REST HAVE "CLOVELLY" ON THEM.

Report Description

Reported Spill Volume: 35000 cubic ft
Report Description/// THIS IS A 48 HOUR UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1404408 /// /// THE UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS /// THE CALLER REPORTED THAT THE QUANTITY RELEASED HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 35,000 STANDARD CUBIC FEET OF NATURAL GAS. THE TEMPORARY LOSS OF WELL CONTROL HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO BE DUE TO A LEAKING PACKING PLUG WHICH CAUSED PRESSURES TO RISE, CAUSING THE TUBING TO EJECT FROM THE BOP STACK. THE TUBING AND THE INFLATABLE BRIDGE PLUG HAVE BEEN REMOVED FROM THE SITE. PRESSURE WAS NOT EQUALIZED FROM BETWEEN BELOW THE BRIDGE PLUG AND THE BOP STACK, WHICH IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT. /// ORIGINAL REPORT BELOW /// THE CALLER REPORTED A RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF NATURAL GAS FROM AN UNDERGROUND WELL INTO THE ATMOSPHERE AT THE INCIDENT LOCATION. THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE IS DUE TO THE TUBING BLOWING OUT OF THE WELL DURING INSTALLATION OF THE TUBING. THE CALLER BELIEVES THEIR WAS A BUILD UP OF PRESSURE IN THE WELL THAT CAUSED THE RELEASE, AND IT IS BELIEVED TO BE DUE TO EQUIPMENT FAILURE. THERE IS A PLUG IN THE WELL THAT IS USED TO PREVENT BUILDUP, AND THEY BELIEVE THE PLUG FAILED.
